newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. Marines take rape appeal to Japan's top court.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Marines take rape appeal to Japan's top court.

text.p: Two of the three U.S. servicemen sentenced for gang raping a schoolgirl in Okinawa last year are appealing their sentences to Japan's Supreme Court, a court spokesman said on Friday.

"The defendants appealed the case," the spokesman for the Naha branch of the Fukuoka High Court told Reuters. "It will probably take about two months for the trial to start at the Supreme Court," he said.
On Thursday, the Fukuoka High Court rejected appeals by Marine privates Rodrico Harp, 22, and Kendrick Ledet, 21, against their sentences for the abduction and rape of the girl on September 4, 1995.
Harp had been sentenced to seven years and Ledet to six and a half years.
Navy Seaman Marcus Gill, 23, who was sentenced to seven years, has not appealed and is serving his sentence in Okinawa.
The rape became a lightning rod for criticism by residents against the lopsided concentration of U.S. military facilities in Okinawa.

The island, some 1,000 km (625 miles) southwest of Tokyo, is home to three-quarters of the U.S. military facilities in Japan and hosts about half of the 47,000 U.S. military personnel stationed in the country, although it constitutes less than one percent of Japan's total land area.
Following the rape, Okinawa Governor Masahide Ota refused to sign orders for renewal of land lease contracts for U.S. military facilities.
This week he won a promise from Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto that Okinawa would get special funds in the national budget.
